question.text: A trader earns Rs. 5,00,000 from exchange-traded GOI bond futures and incurs Rs. 2,00,000 loss from exchange-traded 91-Day T-Bill futures in the same year. What is the net taxable income from these derivatives?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 302 of the NISM Series IV workbook, exchange-traded interest-rate derivative income/loss is treated as non-speculative business income. Page 304 set-off rules permit netting within non-speculative business income, so Rs. 5,00,000 - Rs. 2,00,000 = Rs. 3,00,000 net taxable business income. The Trap: Rs. 5,00,000 ignores the T-Bill futures loss eligible for set-off. Rs. 7,00,000 incorrectly adds the loss instead of subtracting it. Since both legs are exchange-traded interest-rate derivatives and thus non-speculative business income per page 302, full netting is permitted under page 304. Note: Source-backed treatment applies because both products are exchange-traded interest-rate derivatives per Series IV pages 302-304. OTC derivative losses may be classified differently with different set-off rules.
